executive_view.headline: This dataset covers 4,203 inpatient stays across 12 months, with a 30-day readmission rate of 9.0%, in-hospital mortality of 2.4%, and an average length of stay of 3.72 days.

paragraphs.text: Cardiology accounts for the largest share of total charges among all departments, while total charges fell sharply in Oct 2026 compared with Sep 2026.
All rates reported here are crude and not risk-adjusted, so comparisons across departments or time periods should be interpreted with care.

findings.text: The dataset contains 4,203 stays from 1,707 patients, producing 3,455 discharges over the 12-month period from Nov 2025 to Oct 2026.

Cardiology generated the highest total charges ($41,663,189.13), followed by Orthopedics ($33,207,578.70) and General Medicine ($24,167,064.42); Pulmonology ($21,096,247.88) and Neurology ($14,422,030.35) were lower.

Total charges fell 26.3% from Sep 2026 to Oct 2026; because the data covers only 12 months with no prior-year equivalent, it is not possible to determine whether this is seasonal or a genuine decline.

Per-stay charges vary widely — the median is $22,216.05 while the mean is $32,105.12, and the range runs from $3,500.23 to $827,622.78 — indicating a small number of very high-cost stays pulling the average up.

action_items.action: Investigate the drivers of the Oct 2026 drop in total charges before drawing conclusions or adjusting budgets.
action_items.expected_impact: A 26.3% month-over-month fall is material; confirming whether it is seasonal or structural prevents misinformed planning.

action_items.expected_impact: Outliers flagged in Total Charges could distort department-level comparisons and financial forecasts.

action_items.action: Risk-adjust the 9.0% readmission rate and 2.4% mortality rate before using them for benchmarking or performance reporting.
action_items.expected_impact: Crude rates can mislead if case mix differs across departments or time periods.
